obligations.note: Payments privileged idle is set to 16 in policy.py and policy-params.json, above the catalog bound of 15 minutes. EXC-0230, which would allow a sixteen-minute interval, expired on 2026-10-11, before review on 2026-10-12; EXC-0141 is also expired and limited to reconciliation service accounts.
The change names ticket CHG-25115, approved by change manager Grace Kim on 2026-10-07, before review. Its components, payments.policy and payments.controls-data, cover both changed paths.
Sofia Santos, a payments change_approver and not the author, gave a code_review approval of the head commit.
The change is a single commit, and the code_review approval names that commit, df075b361834e93abff397068c5cc794ea104033.

CI run.json records a successful payments suite on the head commit, and the JUnit report shows 172 tests with no failures, errors, or skips, including the unskipped SES-1 control test test_privileged_idle_timeout_within_policy.
The touched components, payments.policy and payments.controls-data, are not marked security_sensitive, so a security review is not required.

controls/payments/policy-params.json is a protected path and this edits an approved policy value. Bao Tran, a control_owner on controls-office, outside the author's payments-eng team, approved control_owner on the head commit.

The sixteen-minute idle interval is a deviation from SES-1, and the cited exception EXC-0230 is expired at review time. It is also recorded against component payments.session, while the change is to payments.policy and payments.controls-data.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers policy.py or policy-params.json, and the paths those entries do cover are unchanged, so prior evidence has not lapsed.

summary: The change raises Payments' privileged session idle limit from 15 minutes to 16 in both the code constant and the approved parameter file. That exceeds SES-1, and the risk exception cited for a sixteen-minute interval expired on 2026-10-11, the day before review. Ticket approval, independent code review, commit coverage, the passing payments suite, and control-owner approval are in place, but they do not cure the expired exception or the parameter breach. The change is rejected.
